explanation: L2 applies the second derivative with respect to s to the expression for F(s). L3 moves differentiation inside the integral. For L4, f(t) is constant with respect to s, and applying the chain rule twice to e^{-st} gives (-t)^2e^{-st}=t^2e^{-st}.

answers.correct_value: the definition of the second derivative with respect to $s$
